title: Secrets & Environment Variables
definition: Encrypted environment variables that you create in an organization, repository, or repository environment. They are used to safely pass passwords, tokens, and SSH keys to GitHub Actions.
simpleExplanation: If your automated robot needs to deploy your website to AWS, it needs your AWS password. If you hardcode the password into the `deploy.yml` file, the whole internet will see it. Instead, you save the password secretly in the GitHub UI, and the robot dynamically injects it into the script at runtime.
realWorldExample: Storing `DATABASE_URL` or `NPM_TOKEN` securely so your CI pipeline can authenticate with third-party services.

basic: Can you view a secret's value in the GitHub UI after you save it?
intermediate: If a script prints a secret using `console.log(process.env.SECRET)`, what shows up in the Action logs?

answers.question: View secret?
answers.answer: No! Once a secret is saved, it is permanently encrypted. You can only update it or delete it. You can never reveal the text again.

answers.question: Console.log secret?
answers.answer: GitHub intercepts it! The log will output `***`. GitHub actively censors your secrets from the logs to prevent accidental leaks.

terminalOutput:
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml

jobs:
  deploy-to-aws:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Deploy Script
        run: ./deploy.sh
        # Injecting the secrets into the environment safely!
        env:
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY }}
          AWS_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_KEY }}
